# CCMR Weekly Workbook — FAQ

*Answers to common questions about the workbook, the data, and how to use it. For a quick start, see the [One-Pager Guide](CCMR-On-Track-Weekly_One-Pager.md).*

---

## Getting started

### How do I get the workbook, and how often?
You receive a refreshed workbook on your campus's configured weekly schedule. Delivery location is set during district onboarding (commonly Google Drive, Box, or a shared folder). Automated email may not work for some districts due to server-side restrictions, so confirm your delivery method with your district contact.

### How do I confirm I'm looking at the right file?
Check the **Menu tab**, which shows your campus name and the week (e.g., "Lake Travis HS — 3/31/2026"). Always save the workbook to your team's shared location so everyone works from the same copy.

---

## Using the workbook

### How do I filter to just my caseload?
The **Counselors** and **Advisors** tabs give you caseload-level rollups by employee. 


### What's the recommended way to use it each week?
Orient (what changed), diagnose (who needs attention), act (assign interventions with clear owners), and revisit the same view next week to check movement. A 15–30 minute weekly meeting is the intended rhythm.

### Can I build a list to hand off to staff?
Yes. Filter All Data to the students you care about, then copy/paste into an email or a separate tracker. The workbook is designed to support action assignment even when the assignment itself happens outside the file.

### Why don't my filters on one tab change the Summary?
By design. Filters apply **only within the current tab.** The Summary always reflects the full campus so it stays a stable reference point. Charts within a tab will update as you filter that tab.

---

## Understanding the data

### What does "TSI Met" mean and how is it determined?
TSI Met indicates a student has demonstrated college readiness in **Math and/or ELAR** under the Texas Success Initiative. The workbook calculates it from the **highest qualifying score** a student has across TSIA2, SAT, or ACT, compared against the state cut scores:

| Assessment | Math | ELAR |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TSIA2 | CRC ≥ 950 | CRC ≥ 945 **and** Essay ≥ 5 |
| SAT | Math ≥ 530 | EBRW ≥ 480 |
| ACT | Math ≥ 19 | English ≥ 19 |

A student is **TSI Met overall** when **both** Math and ELAR are met. A "Met by" label shows which test satisfied each subject (priority order: TSIA2 → SAT → ACT).

### Why did a number change from last week?
The workbook refreshes weekly from upstream sources, so changes are expected and usually good news — new scores posted, an application got submitted, a FAFSA was completed, or a record was corrected at the source. The "Updated" dates on the Menu tab show how current each feed is. If a change looks wrong rather than just new, report it (see below).

### Where does each data point come from?
Each tab indicates its sources, and the Menu tab lists source feeds with their last-updated dates. Data flows from district and college systems through the Regional Data Hub into the workbook. 

---

## Trust, quality, and troubleshooting

### Why are some columns hidden?
Columns are hidden when the underlying data is either **not available** or **not yet reliable** for your campus. Hiding them keeps the workbook credible and prevents decisions based on bad data. As data quality improves, hidden columns can be turned back on.

### What do I do when a student record looks incorrect?
Don't act on the questionable value. Submit a ticket through the support portal (the **Get Help** tab) with the student and field in question. Corrections are made upstream in the source systems, not by editing the workbook — editing your copy won't fix it and the change will be overwritten at the next refresh.

### Can I edit the workbook?
You can filter, sort, and copy data freely, and you can keep your own notes. But remember the file is **regenerated each week**, so any edits you make to the data or layout won't carry forward. Track assignments and notes in a separate place if you need them to persist.

### Which fields are calculated versus reported directly?
TSI Met (Math, ELAR, Overall), the "Met by" labels, GPA bands, and some readiness/college-prep labels are **calculated inside the workbook.** Most other fields (roster, demographics, scores, EOC results, pipeline status) are reported directly from source data. Calculated fields use consistent definitions week to week so you don't have to reinterpret them each refresh.

### Will the workbook always have the same tabs?
Release 1 includes Menu, Summary, All Data, TSI By Assessment, Counselors, Advisors, and Grade Levels. **Release 2** adds more topic tabs (CCMR Status/Trends, IBC Progress, Advanced Coursework, Dual Credit, College Credentials, Postsecondary Enrollment/Pipeline, and Path Form Completion). New tabs are added without breaking existing ones.

---

## Privacy and confidentiality

### How sensitive is this data?
Very. It contains protected student information and is labeled **"HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL DATA — For use by campus leadership, college advisors, and counselors only."** Sharing it outside authorized users is prohibited and the product is operated under FERPA-aligned controls.

### Who do I contact with questions?
Submit a ticket through the **support portal** (the **Get Help** tab in the workbook). The portal covers everything — data corrections, access and confidentiality questions, product or usage issues, and clarifications about how a field is calculated or sourced.

# Enrollment Pipeline Navigator (EPN) FAQ 

## What is the EPN?
The Enrollment Pipeline Navigator is a dashboard and reporting tool that helps enrollment teams identify students at risk of not enrolling in college and take timely action to support them. It integrates data from multiple district and college systems to provide a consolidated view of student progress.

## Who is it for?
The primary users are Enrollment Managers and Senior Enrollment Managers responsible for ensuring students successfully transition from high school to college. Secondary users include program teams and leadership.

## What are the key benefits?
- Quickly identify students needing additional support through risk indicators and key progress metrics
- Assign and track interventions to help get students back on track 
- Spend less time collating spreadsheets and more time assisting students
- Analyze trends and evaluate impact at the campus, grade, and caseload level

## What data does it provide?
The EPN dashboard and student detail views surface critical enrollment milestones such as:

- College application submission (ApplyTexas, CommonApp, etc.)
- FAFSA/TASFA completion status 
- Pre-registration steps like orientation attendance, placement tests, and advising
- Enrollment verification and course registration  

It also calculates key risk indicators like "College Enrollment Not On Track" which factor in multiple data points to flag students needing intervention.

All data can be filtered by campus, grade level, counselor/advisor, student group, or custom tags. Enrollment Managers can hone in on just their caseloads while leadership can monitor the full pipeline.  

## Where does the data come from and how often is it refreshed? 
Data is pulled weekly from district source systems and college partners through the Regional Data Hub. This includes:

- District SIS (student roster, demographics, HS academics) 
- State higher ed data (ApplyTexas, THECB reports)
- College application and enrollment feeds
- Financial aid databases (FAFSA, TASFA)

The date of the most recent refresh is shown on each dashboard so you know how current the data is. Risk indicators and KPIs are calculated using standardized logic so you can accurately track progress over time.

## How do I use it?
The basic weekly flow is to:
1. Check the Summary dashboard to gauge overall progress and week-over-week changes
2. Review key student watchlists (e.g. College Applications Missing, FAFSA Incomplete) to identify students for outreach  
3. Log interventions and assign owners for prioritized student groups
4. Monitor progress at your next team meeting to assess intervention effectiveness

Use the filter options to generate custom rosters to share with your team for targeted student support. You can also log notes directly on student profiles to capture discussion takeaways and next steps.

## What if I see missing or incorrect data?
Report data issues or discrepancies through the in-app Support Portal (help icon in the top right). Since data is sourced directly from district and college systems, corrections are made in those systems first. The EPN will reflect updates on the next weekly refresh.


## What's next?  
The EPN is rolling out to initial pilot districts this spring with broader access coming this summer ahead of peak enrollment season. Your district leadership will receive regular updates on the rollout plan.

Once launched, the tool will continue to evolve based on user feedback and data from additional partners will be integrated over time. Review the Roadmap in the EPN's Documentation tab to see planned enhancements.
